prompt: Some people think it is a good thing for senior managers to have much higher salaries than other workers in a company. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
More and more people think that executives should receive much higher wages than the remaining employees. While some individuals agree with this opinion, others argue that it brings more drawbacks. In my opinion, I partially agree that the advantages are more than the drawbacks for two main reasons.

On one hand, there are several advantages to raising the salary of the manager; for instance, this encourages staff to perform better. In addition, when each employee enhances their performance, this will affect the company in a positive way. Market observations consistently show that the prospect of a greater salary is a primary cause of staff ambition, driving employees to improve their skills in pursuit of executive roles. Therefore, there is a clear relation between a high wage and good performance. From my perspective, the main reason why managers have high salaries is the responsibility; for example, they will be responsible for any reduction in production.

On the other hand, having a much more substantial salary than others could lead some workers to feel a sense of injustice. Furthermore, there are other jobs which could be harder than a manager that may deter many people from different fields. The solution for this issue, based on past experiences, is increasing the salaries of these fields and ensuring that the gap between them and the managers does not exceed 40%.

In conclusion, I think the executives around the world are supposed to receive elevated wages due to the performance and the responsibility they hold, but the difference between them and the remaining staff should be controlled.
